title: How do I ask for help in an emergency in English?
L: (1) Minh: I'm moving to the US soon. How do I ask for help in English in an emergency?
(2) Sara: First, call 911. Stay calm and speak slowly.
The operator will ask, “What is your emergency?” Say what happened, like “My friend fainted.”
Then give your address or the name of a nearby street.
Don't hang up until the operator says you can.
(3) Ravi: I'd add one more thing: save your home address in your phone.
It's easy to forget it when you're scared.
Also, learn a few short phrases, like “I need an ambulance” and “Please hurry.”
(4) Minh: Thanks, both of you! I'll practice these phrases tonight.

exq.q: Why is Minh asking for help?
exq.a: He wants to know how to call for help in English.
w: He lost his phone in the US.
He is looking for a flight to the US.
exq.why: “How do I ask for help in English in an emergency?”

exq.q: What should callers do first, according to Sara?
w: Go to a hospital by bus
Wait for the police to call

exq.q: Why does Ravi say Minh should save his address in his phone?
exq.a: It is easy to forget it when you are scared.
w: The operator needs his phone number.
exq.why: “It’s easy to forget it when you’re scared.”

exq.q: What does Sara say about hanging up?
exq.a: Do not hang up until the operator says you can.
w: Hang up as soon as you give your name.
Hang up if the operator is slow.
exq.why: “Don’t hang up until the operator says you can.”
